request.spec:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can archive the sheet (a button; SHEET_ARCHIVED; anyone else is refused with an error
on the sheet). Show archived yes/no. On an archived sheet everything stays visible and every
change is refused with its usual error, including changing the sheet's today, every bulk action,
the paste box and the quick-add bar.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sheet archiving is in place and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What it does**
- **Storage:** a new migration `V42__sheet_archived.sql` adds an `archived` flag to each sheet, off by default. The sheet data the screen reads now includes it.
- **Archiving:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/archive`. A steward (including someone the steward role is delegated to) can archive the sheet, and it writes `SHEET_ARCHIVED sheet=<id> by=<user>` to the audit file. Anyone else is refused, and so is archiving a sheet that's already archived. A refusal writes nothing.
- **Blocking changes:** `CheckCanChange` already runs first on every change endpoint, so I added the archived check there. On an archived sheet that refuses changing today, rates, settings, roles, delegations, periods, people, claims, the paste box, the quick-add bar and archiving again, each showing its usual error. The bulk open and bulk settle actions don't go through that check, so on an archived sheet they now report every selected claim as refused.
- **Screen:** next to Today, the sheet panel shows "Archived: yes/no" (`sheet-archived`) and an "Archive sheet" button (`sheet-archive`). A refusal shows in `sheet-error`, which clears on the next archive or change to today.

**Decisions for you**
- **Watching is still allowed on an archived sheet.** Watching a person is the user's own setting and doesn't change the sheet's data, so I left it out of the check. Viewers can already watch, so this matches. If "every change" should include it, it's a one-line addition to the watch endpoint.
- **Archiving can't be undone.** The request didn't ask for unarchiving, so there's no way to reverse it.

The first test took 40 seconds against about 20 for the others. It passed, and I didn't look into why it was slower.
